nodes.title: SG-2.1 Typed manifest interfaces and zod validators
nodes.body:
Context: game/ has a yaml-only runtime (game/package.json) with src/content, engine, state and systems, but no src/assets folder. Desired behavior: a typed asset manifest module with zod runtime validators covering asset id, path, type, dimensions, spritesheet frames, animations, origin/anchor and interaction bounds. Expected result: later cycles can validate manifest JSON without touching the engine. Why: AI-friendly, validated content architecture.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given game/package.json, when read, then zod is declared as a dependency
- Given a valid manifest object, when validated, then typed data is returned
- Given an invalid manifest object, when validated, then a failure naming the bad field path is returned
- Given the module, when imported, then TypeScript interfaces exist for id, path, type, dimensions, frames, animations, origin and interaction bounds


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/manifest schemas, types and validators
- In scope: zod dependency in game/package.json
- Out of scope: Manifest loader and reference checks
- Out of scope: Phaser rendering
- Out of scope: Authoring the-boys-room manifest content
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Preserve: Existing game/src/content, engine, state and systems behavior
- Preserve: yaml dependency


## Technical constraints
- Use zod as runtime validator
- TypeScript strict, ESM, Bundler resolution
- Files live under game/src/assets/manifest


## Definition of done
- All three requirements delivered and verified by unit tests


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Typed manifest schemas cover id, path, type, dimensions, frames, animations, origin and bounds
nodes.body:
Context: no manifest types exist. Desired behavior: zod schemas defining an asset entry (id, path, type, dimensions, optional spritesheet frame info, animations, origin/anchor, interaction bounds) and a manifest wrapper, with TypeScript types inferred from them. Expected result: one source of truth for types and validation. Why: typed content contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a valid image asset entry, when parsed by assetSchema, then it succeeds
- Given a spritesheet asset with frameWidth, frameHeight and animations referencing frame indices, when parsed, then it succeeds
- Given an entry with non-positive dimensions or an unknown type, when parsed, then it fails
- Given origin values outside 0..1 or negative bounds size, when parsed, then it fails


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/manifest/schema.ts
- Out of scope: Loading files
- Out of scope: Cross-asset reference checks
- Preserve: Existing src modules


## Technical constraints
- Types via z.infer
- Asset types: image, spritesheet, audio


## Dependencies
- REQ1


## Definition of done
- Schemas and types exported


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Runtime validators return typed data or path-named errors without throwing
nodes.body:
Context: schemas alone throw on failure. Desired behavior: validator functions return a discriminated result with typed data or an error list naming field paths, plus duplicate asset id detection, exported via index.ts. Expected result: callers can validate untrusted manifest JSON safely. Why: handle bad content gracefully.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a valid manifest, when parseManifest runs, then ok is true and data is typed
- Given an invalid manifest, when parseManifest runs, then ok is false and errors contain the failing field path
- Given two assets with the same id, when parseManifest runs, then ok is false and an error names the duplicate id
- Given non-object input, when parseManifest runs, then it returns ok false without throwing


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/manifest/validate.ts
- In scope: game/src/assets/manifest/index.ts
- Out of scope: Filesystem loading
- Preserve: Existing src modules


## Technical constraints
- Use safeParse


## Dependencies
- REQ2


## Definition of done
- Validators and index exported


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.description: Create game/src/assets/manifest/schema.ts defining schemas and exported inferred types.
acceptance_criteria: Module exports assetSchema and manifestSchema as zod schemas
Module exports types AssetEntry, AssetManifest, AnimationDef, FrameSpec and InteractionBounds

steps.action: Create the file importing { z } from 'zod'. Define dimensionsSchema {width,height} as positive ints; originSchema {x,y} numbers 0..1; boundsSchema {x,y numbers, width,height positive numbers}; frameSpecSchema {frameWidth,frameHeight positive ints, frameCount positive int, optional margin,spacing non-negative ints}; animationSchema {frames: nonempty array of non-negative ints, frameRate positive number, repeat int >= -1 default -1}; assetSchema {id nonempty string, path nonempty string, type enum image|spritesheet|audio, dimensions optional, frames optional, animations optional record of animationSchema, origin optional, interactionBounds optional}; manifestSchema {version literal 1, assets array of assetSchema}. Add superRefine on assetSchema: type spritesheet requires frames and dimensions. Export z.infer types AssetEntry, AssetManifest, AnimationDef, FrameSpec, InteractionBounds, Origin, Dimensions
steps.expected: Module compiles and exports schemas and types

nodes.description: Implement non-throwing validators using the schemas and export the public API.
acceptance_criteria: parseManifest returns {ok:true,data} or {ok:false,errors}
Duplicate asset ids are reported in the errors list

steps.action: Import manifestSchema, assetSchema and types from ./schema. Export type ValidationResult<T> = {ok:true;data:T}|{ok:false;errors:string[]}. parseAsset(input: unknown) uses assetSchema.safeParse and maps issues to `${issue.path.join('.')}: ${issue.message}`. parseManifest(input: unknown) uses manifestSchema.safeParse, same mapping, then on success collects duplicate asset ids and returns ok:false with error `duplicate asset id: <id>` for each
steps.expected: Functions never throw for any input

steps.action: Re-export everything from ./schema and ./validate with export * statements
steps.expected: Importing game/src/assets/manifest exposes schemas, types and validators
